q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this systematically.

**(a) Time left until resolution**

Today is 2026-08-23. NVIDIA reports Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. That's **3 days** until the earnings release. This is an extremely short timeframe where the outcome is largely predetermined.

**(b) Most likely outcome and why**

NVIDIA has already issued forward guidance on May 20, 2026, projecting Q2 FY2027 revenue of **$91.0 billion ±2%** (range: $89.18B to $92.82B).

The question asks: "What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release?"

This phrasing is slightly ambiguous—it could mean:
1. What will NVIDIA's actual reported Q2 FY2027 revenue be (already given guidance)?
2. What forward guidance will they issue for Q3 FY2027?

Given the context and that we're 3 days before the release, I interpret this as asking for **NVIDIA's actual Q2 FY2027 revenue result** they will report in the earnings call. The company has already guided to $91.0B ±2%.

Historically, NVIDIA has beaten guidance:
- Q1 FY2027: Reported $81.6B, beat midpoint guidance by 4.6% (guidance was ~$78B midpoint)
- Wall Street consensus is $91.9B (slightly above NVIDIA's $91.0B midpoint)

NVIDIA's recent track record shows they tend to beat their own guidance while meeting or slightly exceeding analyst consensus.

**(c) What would push the value lower?**

- Unexpected weakness in data center demand in the final weeks of Q2
- Supply chain disruptions in the final days
- Macro deterioration impacting customer orders
- Conservative beats (i.e., they guided to $91B but came in lower—unlikely but possible)
- Unexpected China-related headwinds beyond what's already baked into guidance

**(d) What would push the value higher?**

- NVIDIA's historical pattern of beating guidance (4.6% in Q1)
- Strong demand from AI/data center customers leading to better-than-expected bookings
- Upside from products like automotive or other segments
- Wall Street consensus already at $91.9B suggests analysts expect upside
- If they did beat by a similar margin as Q1 (4.6%), that would put them at ~$95.2B

**(e) Base rate or historical reference values**

From the research provided:
- Q1 FY2027 reported: **$81.6 billion** (beat guidance by 4.6%)
- Q2 FY2027 NVIDIA guidance: **$91.0 billion ±2%** ($89.18B–$92.82B)
- Wall Street consensus for Q2: **$91.9 billion** (~0.9-1% above NVIDIA's midpoint)
- Q3 FY2027 consensus: **$103.1 billion**

**Analysis:**

With only 3 days until the release, the actual result is almost fully determined. NVIDIA's guidance range of $89.18B–$92.82B is tight. Wall Street consensus at $91.9B sits comfortably within that range, slightly above midpoint.

Given NVIDIA's track record of beating guidance (Q1 beat by 4.6%), I'd expect them to come in slightly above their $91.0B midpoint. However, there's a 2% margin of error built into their guidance, suggesting they're confident in a tight range.

The most likely outcome is somewhere between:
- Lower bound of their guidance: $89.18B (very unlikely they miss to the downside)
- Midpoint of their guidance: $91.0B (base case if they hit exactly)
- 4-5% beat like Q1: $95.2B (upper scenario based on precedent)

Distribution:
- 10th percentile (very low): $89.5B (near lower bound of guidance)
- 50th percentile (median): $92.0B (slightly above midpoint, in line with analyst consensus and modest beat)
- 90th percentile (high): $94.5B (strong beat like Q1 pattern)

Low (10th percentile): 89500000000
Median (50th percentile): 92000000000
High (90th percentile): 94500000000
q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to report its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The company's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, projects Q2 FY2027 revenue to be \$91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/). This guidance explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/).

Wall Street analysts, based on 40 to 42 estimates, currently forecast NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 revenue to be around \$91.9 billion, with some sources citing \$91.85 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). This analyst consensus sits about 0.9% to 1% above the midpoint of NVIDIA's own guidance [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported \$81.6 billion in revenue, beating its own midpoint guidance by 4.6% and analyst consensus by 5.5% [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/).

The consensus revenue forecast for Q3 FY2027 is \$103.1 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/).
